newsitem.title: USA: NYS gov plans new rent rules, will protect tenants.
newsitem.headline: NYS gov plans new rent rules, will protect tenants.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, who has seen his budget get bogged down in a brutal battle over rent rules for apartments and who has promised to broker a deal, said Wednesday he would soon unveil his plan.

"Within the next week, I will offer a proposal that should move us forward, protecting every New York City tenant who should be protected, while strengthening the system," Pataki said, in prepared remarks.
No further information about the Republican governor's plan was immediately available.

Pataki attacked his main Democrat opponent in the fight over rent-regulated apartments, saying Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver's attempt to link the rules to property tax relief was a poor idea. "It divides New Yorkers by regions and I oppose that."

A spokeswoman for Silver said the Manhattan Democrat was looking forward to seeing the details of the governor's plan. "We are interested in seeing how he would go about protecting the 2.7 million middle-class families (in rent-regulated apartments)," said Pat Lynch. New York City has the lion's share of the state's rent-regulated apartments.

She added that the Speaker's remarks about linking rent rules to tax abatements for landlords had been misinterpreted. "It was never linked. What the speaker was saying was that in the context of negotiations, we have to look at various incentives to allow landlords to continue building."

State Senator Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, has threatened to allow the rent rules to expire on June 15 unless an accord were reached on phasing the rules out over a two- or possibly four-year period, while protecting elderly, disabled and needy tenants. The Assembly approved a bill to make the present system permanent, putting it in conflict with the Senate and the governor, who previously has said he favored vacancy decontrol.
